answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a verifiable history of useful work that cannot be copied cheaply. Like layers of shale and basalt forming an island over time, reputation should accumulate only through completed tasks, peer attestations, and staked deposits that are slashed for fraud. Creating thousands of fake agents then requires real computation, real collateral, and a long record for every identity, so the cost of forging a crowd exceeds any reward from manipulating one vote or market.
